title: Mate y facturas en la costanera

dialogue.speaker: Micaela
dialogue.spanish: Che, Nico, mirá qué lindo solcito hay hoy en la costanera. ¿Trajiste el termo con agua caliente?
dialogue.english: Hey, Nico, look what lovely sunshine there is on the waterfront today. Did you bring the thermos with hot water?

dialogue.speaker: Nico
dialogue.spanish: ¡Olvidate! Está a ochenta grados, ideal para cebar unos buenos mates amargos.
dialogue.english: You bet! It's at eighty degrees, ideal for brewing some good unsweetened mates.

slang.actualMeaning: You bet! / Of course! / Definitely! (enthusiastic Argentine affirmation)

dialogue.speaker: Micaela
dialogue.spanish: Bueno, yo pasé recién por la panadería del barrio y compré una docena de facturas con dulce de leche.
dialogue.english: Well, I just stopped by the neighborhood bakery and bought a dozen pastries with dulce de leche.

slang.actualMeaning: sweet bakery pastries (in Argentina, 'facturas' at a bakery are pastries!)
slang.example: Traje una docena de facturas para tomar el mate en la tarde.

dialogue.speaker: Nico
dialogue.spanish: ¡Sos una genia total! O sea, hacía toda la semana que tenía ganas de comer vigilantes y medialunas.
dialogue.english: You're an absolute legend! I mean, all week long I've been craving pastries and croissants.

dialogue.speaker: Micaela
dialogue.spanish: Sentémonos en ese banco de madera frente al río que corre una brisa divina.
dialogue.english: Let's sit on that wooden bench facing the river where there's a lovely breeze.

dialogue.speaker: Nico
dialogue.spanish: Dale, pero ojo con el primer mate que siempre sale un poco fuerte y caliente, ¿viste?
dialogue.english: Sure, just watch out for the first mate since it always comes out a bit strong and hot, you know?

questions.question: Where are Micaela and Nico spending the afternoon?
options: On a wooden bench facing the river along the waterfront ('la costanera')
questions.explanation: They are at 'la costanera' (the waterfront) and sit on 'ese banco de madera frente al río.'

questions.question: What did Micaela buy at the neighborhood bakery to share with the mate?
options: A dozen pastries ('facturas') with dulce de leche
A bag of apples and oranges
questions.explanation: Micaela says: 'compré una docena de facturas con dulce de leche.'

questions.question: What does Nico warn Micaela about at the end?
options: The first mate always comes out a bit strong and hot
The water in the thermos is already cold
The seagulls might steal their pastries
The park closes at five o'clock
questions.explanation: Nico warns: 'ojo con el primer mate que siempre sale un poco fuerte y caliente.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: When Nico says '¡Olvidate!' and Micaela mentions 'una docena de facturas', what do they mean in Argentina?
options: '¡Olvidate!' = You bet / Of course!; 'facturas' = sweet bakery pastries
questions.explanation: In Argentina, '¡Olvidate!' is an enthusiastic 'You bet / Of course!' (not 'I forgot!'), and 'facturas' are bakery pastries!
